title: Boots are at the ends of his legs, nebeneinander
html_source: Mulligan and Stephen have conjoined as Blake and Milton did in Blake’s poem Milton. Joyce’s meaning lies not in Proteus but in Blake. Blake suggested he could transcend the ties which bind literature by extending the nacheinander form into his visionary creations, accessing the nebeneinander. Stephen’s feet, in borrowed tatty shoes joining with Mulligan’s legs as a launchpad to the eternal is pushing it a bit. Joyce mocks literature and reveals Stephen isn’t completely up himself to further our understanding of his plight.
